claim: SNX27 is linked to various neuropathologies through sorting of integral proteins to the synaptic surface, most notably AMPA receptors.
source: The endosome-associated cargo adaptor sorting nexin-27 (SNX27) is linked to various neuropathologies through sorting of integral proteins to the synaptic surface, most notably AMPA receptors.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known fact about SNX27's role in neuropathologies.

claim: Proteomics in rat primary neurons identified SNX27-dependent cargoes linked to excitotoxicity, epilepsy, intellectual disabilities, and working memory deficits.
source: To provide a broader view of SNX27-associated pathologies, we performed proteomics in rat primary neurons to identify SNX27-dependent cargoes, and identified proteins linked to excitotoxicity, epilepsy, intellectual disabilities, and working memory deficits.
evidence: The abstract describes the proteomic approach and the types of proteins identified.

claim: SNX27 binds to LRFN2 and regulates its endosomal sorting.
source: Focusing on the synaptic adhesion molecule LRFN2, we established that SNX27 binds to LRFN2 and regulates its endosomal sorting.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding about the SNX27-LRFN2 interaction.

claim: LRFN2 associates with AMPA receptors.
source: Furthermore, LRFN2 associates with AMPA receptors and knockdown of LRFN2 results in decreased surface AMPA receptor expression, reduced synaptic activity, and attenuated hippocampal long-term potentiation.
evidence: The abstract states this association as a finding from the study.

claim: Knockdown of LRFN2 results in decreased surface AMPA receptor expression.
source: Furthermore, LRFN2 associates with AMPA receptors and knockdown of LRFN2 results in decreased surface AMPA receptor expression, reduced synaptic activity, and attenuated hippocampal long-term potentiation.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this experimental result.

claim: Knockdown of LRFN2 results in reduced synaptic activity.
source: Furthermore, LRFN2 associates with AMPA receptors and knockdown of LRFN2 results in decreased surface AMPA receptor expression, reduced synaptic activity, and attenuated hippocampal long-term potentiation.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this experimental result.

claim: Knockdown of LRFN2 results in attenuated hippocampal long-term potentiation.
source: Furthermore, LRFN2 associates with AMPA receptors and knockdown of LRFN2 results in decreased surface AMPA receptor expression, reduced synaptic activity, and attenuated hippocampal long-term potentiation.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this experimental result.

claim: SNX27 controls AMPA receptor-mediated synaptic transmission and plasticity indirectly through the sorting of LRFN2.
source: Overall, our study provides an additional mechanism by which SNX27 can control AMPA receptor-mediated synaptic transmission and plasticity indirectly through the sorting of LRFN2 and offers molecular insight into the perturbed function of SNX27 and LRFN2 in a range of neurological conditions.
evidence: The abstract presents this as a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: The endosomal network controls the functionality of the cell surface through orchestrating the sorting of endocytosed integral proteins between degradation within the lysosome or retrieval from degradation for active recycling back to the plasma membrane.
source: The endosomal network plays a central role in controlling the functionality of the cell surface through orchestrating the sorting of endocytosed integral proteins between two fates: either degradation within the lysosome or retrieval from degradation for active recycling back to the plasma membrane (Cullen and Steinberg, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Cullen and Steinberg, 2018.

claim: Sorting nexins were identified as core and evolutionarily conserved sorting complexes that orchestrate retrieval and recycling.
source: While the molecular details of sorting to the degradative fate are relatively well described, only recently, with the identification of sorting nexins (Kurten et al., 1996; Stockinger et al., 2002; Joubert et al., 2004; Carlton et al., 2004; Strochlic et al., 2007; Harterink et al., 2011), retromer (Seaman et al., 1998), retriever (McNally et al., 2017), and the WASH, CCC and ESCPE-1 complexes (Derivery et al., 2009; Gomez and Billadeau, 2009; Phillips-Krawczak et al., 2015; Simonetti et al., 2019), have the core and evolutionarily conserved sorting complexes that orchestrate retrieval and recycling begun to be identified.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published work.

claim: Mutations in sorting complexes are linked with a variety of human pathologies, most notably neurological diseases and disorders, metabolic conditions and pathogen infections.
source: Importantly, an increasing body of clinical evidence is linking mutations in these sorting complexes with a variety of human pathologies, most notably neurological diseases and disorders, metabolic conditions and pathogen infections (Cullen and Steinberg, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Cullen and Steinberg, 2018.

claim: Destabilised expression of SNX27 is associated with Down's Syndrome.
source: A case in point is sorting nexin-27 (SNX27), in which destabilised expression is associated with Down's Syndrome and coding mutations are observed in patients with pleomorphic phenotypes that have at their core epilepsy, developmental delay and subcortical white matter abnormalities (Damseh et al., 2015; Parente et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Damseh et al., 2015; Parente et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2013.

claim: Coding mutations in SNX27 are observed in patients with pleomorphic phenotypes that have at their core epilepsy, developmental delay and subcortical white matter abnormalities.
source: A case in point is sorting nexin-27 (SNX27), in which destabilised expression is associated with Down's Syndrome and coding mutations are observed in patients with pleomorphic phenotypes that have at their core epilepsy, developmental delay and subcortical white matter abnormalities (Damseh et al., 2015; Parente et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Damseh et al., 2015; Parente et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2013.

claim: SNX27 contains an amino-terminal PSD-95, Disc-large and ZO-1 (PDZ) domain.
source: SNX27 is unique within the sorting nexin family in that it contains an amino-terminal PSD-95, Disc-large and ZO-1 (PDZ) domain.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the structure of SNX27.

claim: The PDZ domain of SNX27 mediates binding to the heterotrimeric retromer complex.
source: This serves a bifunctional role mediating two mutually exclusive protein:protein interactions: first, the binding to the heterotrimeric retromer complex (Gallon et al., 2014; Steinberg et al., 2013); and secondly, the binding to a specific type of PDZ domain-binding motif located at the carboxy-terminus of an array of integral proteins (Cullen, 2008; Steinberg et al., 2013; Lauffer et al., 2010; Temkin et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Gallon et al., 2014; Steinberg et al., 2013.

claim: The PDZ domain of SNX27 mediates binding to a specific type of PDZ domain-binding motif located at the carboxy-terminus of an array of integral proteins.
source: This serves a bifunctional role mediating two mutually exclusive protein:protein interactions: first, the binding to the heterotrimeric retromer complex (Gallon et al., 2014; Steinberg et al., 2013); and secondly, the binding to a specific type of PDZ domain-binding motif located at the carboxy-terminus of an array of integral proteins (Cullen, 2008; Steinberg et al., 2013; Lauffer et al., 2010; Temkin et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Cullen, 2008; Steinberg et al., 2013; Lauffer et al., 2010; Temkin et al., 2011.

claim: SNX27 regulates the retromer-dependent retrieval of internalised integral proteins that contain the specific PDZ domain-binding motif and promotes their recycling to the plasma membrane.
source: Through these interactions SNX27 regulates the retromer-dependent retrieval of internalised integral proteins that contain the specific PDZ domain-binding motif and promotes their recycling to the plasma membrane (Lauffer et al., 2010; Temkin et al., 2011; Steinberg et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Lauffer et al., 2010; Temkin et al., 2011; Steinberg et al., 2013.

claim: SNX27 regulates the trafficking of α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) receptors.
source: These proteins include α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) receptors (Wang et al., 2013; Hussain et al., 2014; Loo et al., 2014), N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors (Cai et al., 2011), serotonin (5-HT) receptors (Joubert et al., 2004) and the G protein–activated inward rectifying potassium channels (GIRK/Kir3) (Lunn et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Wang et al., 2013; Hussain et al., 2014; Loo et al., 2014.

claim: SNX27 regulates the trafficking of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors.
source: These proteins include α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) receptors (Wang et al., 2013; Hussain et al., 2014; Loo et al., 2014), N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors (Cai et al., 2011), serotonin (5-HT) receptors (Joubert et al., 2004) and the G protein–activated inward rectifying potassium channels (GIRK/Kir3) (Lunn et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Cai et al., 2011.

claim: SNX27 regulates the trafficking of serotonin (5-HT) receptors.
source: These proteins include α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) receptors (Wang et al., 2013; Hussain et al., 2014; Loo et al., 2014), N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors (Cai et al., 2011), serotonin (5-HT) receptors (Joubert et al., 2004) and the G protein–activated inward rectifying potassium channels (GIRK/Kir3) (Lunn et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Joubert et al., 2004.

claim: SNX27 regulates the trafficking of G protein–activated inward rectifying potassium channels (GIRK/Kir3).
source: These proteins include α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) receptors (Wang et al., 2013; Hussain et al., 2014; Loo et al., 2014), N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors (Cai et al., 2011), serotonin (5-HT) receptors (Joubert et al., 2004) and the G protein–activated inward rectifying potassium channels (GIRK/Kir3) (Lunn et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Lunn et al., 2007.

claim: SNX27 is required to maintain AMPA-receptor-mediated postsynaptic currents during the process of synaptic plasticity.
source: From studies in SNX27 knockout mice, it is clear that SNX27 is required to maintain AMPA-receptor-mediated postsynaptic currents during the process of synaptic plasticity (Wang et al., 2013; Loo et al., 2014; Cai et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Wang et al., 2013; Loo et al., 2014; Cai et al., 2011.

claim: De-regulation of SNX27 expression associated with Down's syndrome is considered to lead to synaptic dysfunction, in part, through reduced SNX27-mediated AMPA receptor trafficking.
source: Indeed, the de-regulation of SNX27 expression associated with Down's syndrome (Wang et al., 2013), is considered to lead to synaptic dysfunction, in part, through reduced SNX27-mediated AMPA receptor trafficking.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2013 and represents an interpretation of the data.

claim: Clairfeuille and colleagues were unable to detect quantifiable binding of SNX27 to the AMPA receptor subunits GluA1 and GluA2 using isothermal titration calorimetry.
source: However, using isothermal titration calorimetry Clairfeuille and colleagues were unable to detect quantifiable binding of SNX27 to the AMPA receptor subunits GluA1 and GluA2.
evidence: This statement refers to experimental results from Clairfeuille and colleagues.

claim: Clairfeuille and colleagues failed to observe binding between SNX27 and GluA1 upon GluA1 phosphorylation.
source: Moreover, the authors failed to observe binding upon GluA1 phosphorylation, or upon association of SNX27 with the retromer component VPS26, which is known to enhance SNX27 binding to other PDZ binding motif-containing cargoes (Clairfeuille et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement refers to experimental results from Clairfeuille et al., 2016.

claim: Association of SNX27 with the retromer component VPS26 is known to enhance SNX27 binding to other PDZ binding motif-containing cargoes.
source: Moreover, the authors failed to observe binding upon GluA1 phosphorylation, or upon association of SNX27 with the retromer component VPS26, which is known to enhance SNX27 binding to other PDZ binding motif-containing cargoes (Clairfeuille et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Clairfeuille et al., 2016.

claim: GFP-SNX27 retains the ability to localise to endosomes as defined by co-localisation with the early endosomal marker EEA1.
source: Here, we transduced cortical neurons with sindbis virus expressing either GFP or GFP-SNX27 and verified that the GFP-SNX27 retained the ability to localise to endosomes as defined by co-localisation with the early endosomal marker EEA1 (Figure 1A).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: 276 proteins were initially identified as SNX27-interacting proteins by excluding proteins not present in all three datasets.
source: A single list of SNX27-interacting proteins (276 proteins) was initially resolved by excluding proteins not present in all three datasets (Figure 1B and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This statement describes the initial filtering of proteomic data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: 212 proteins comprise a high confidence cortical neuronal SNX27 interactome after further refinement.
source: We further refined these data by excluding proteins that had an average log-fold change of GFP-SNX27:GFP of less than two and removed identified proteins if they did not meet statistical significance (p<0.05). The resulting 212 proteins were considered to comprise a high confidence cortical neuronal SNX27 interactome (Figure 1C and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This statement describes the refined proteomic data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Established SNX27 interactors including the retromer and WASH complexes were identified in the proteomic screen.
source: Confirming the validity of our approach, many established SNX27 interactors were identified including the retromer and WASH complexes (Steinberg et al., 2013) and OTU deubiquitinase with linear linkage specificity (OTULIN) – a deubiquitinase with specificity for Met1-linked ubiquitin chains (Stangl et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Steinberg et al., 2013 and Stangl et al., 2019.

claim: Many of the SNX27 interactors were classified as having a role in neuronal development and differentiation, as well as intracellular transport.
source: We used gene ontology analysis (PANTHER Classification System; p < 0.05) to assess the neuronal SNX27 interactome and found that many of the SNX27 interactors were classified in having a role in neuronal development and differentiation, as well as intracellular transport (Figure 1D).
evidence: This statement is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Sixteen out of 212 identified proteins contained a Type I PDZ binding motif with the optimal acidic amino acid at the −3 position required for high-affinity binding to SNX27.
source: Out of the 212 identified proteins sixteen contained a Type I PDZ binding motif with the optimal acidic amino acid at the −3 position required for high-affinity binding to SNX27 (Clairfeuille et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Clairfeuille et al., 2016.

claim: Seven proteins with Type I PDZ binding motifs were classified as integral proteins: SLC1A3, SLC4A7, SLC6A11, KCNT2, KIDINS220, ADAM22, and LRFN2.
source: Within this cohort, seven proteins were classified as integral proteins (shown in orange in Figure 1C and Supplementary file 1): the high-affinity glutamate transporter, SLC1A3 (Storck et al., 1992) (PDZ binding motif – E−3-T-K-M−0) and the sodium bicarbonate co-transporter, SLC4A7 (Thornell and Bevensee, 2015) (E−3-T-S-L−0); a sodium-dependent transporter, SLC6A11 (Borden, 1996) (E−3-T-H-F−0); an outward rectifying potassium channel, KCNT2 (Bhattacharjee et al., 2003) (E−3-T-Q-L−0); a scaffold in neurotrophin signalling, KIDINS220 (Iglesias et al., 2000; Kong et al., 2001) (E−3-S-I-L−0); a receptor for the neuronal secreted protein LGI1 (Fukata, 2006), ADAM22 (E−3-T-S-I−0), and LRFN2 (E−3-S-T-V−0), a protein previously implicated in the synaptic clustering of glutamate receptors (Ko et al., 2006; Morimura et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2006), and genetically associated with patients harbouring working memory deficits (Thevenon et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations and refers to Figure 1C.

claim: AMPA receptor subunits were not classified as components of the neuronal SNX27 interactome.
source: Interestingly, we failed to classify any AMPA receptor subunits as components of the neuronal SNX27 interactome.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the proteomic results.

claim: GluA2 was quantified in one data set but did not fulfil the stringent filtering criteria.
source: That said, GluA2 was quantified in one data set but did not fulfil the stringent filtering criteria and hence was not annotated in the final interactome.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the proteomic results.

claim: GFP-SLC1A3 and GFP-SLC4A7 efficiently pulled down endogenous SNX27 in a manner dependent on their PDZ binding motifs.
source: While both GFP-SLC1A3 and GFP-SLC4A7 efficiently pulled down endogenous SNX27, in a manner dependent on their PDZ binding motifs (Figure 1F), we failed to observe detectable association of endogenous SNX27 with any of the GFP-tagged AMPA receptor subunits (Figure 1G).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: No detectable association of endogenous SNX27 with any of the GFP-tagged AMPA receptor subunits was observed in HEK293T cells.
source: While both GFP-SLC1A3 and GFP-SLC4A7 efficiently pulled down endogenous SNX27, in a manner dependent on their PDZ binding motifs (Figure 1F), we failed to observe detectable association of endogenous SNX27 with any of the GFP-tagged AMPA receptor subunits (Figure 1G).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: No association of AMPA receptor subunits with rat SNX27 was observed in HEK293T cells expressing Flag-tagged full-length rat SNX27.
source: To ensure that the lack of detectable binding did not arise from species cross reactivity, an unlikely event given the high-sequence conservation between rat and human SNX27, we also performed a series of co-immunoprecipitation experiments in HEK293T cells expressing the GFP-tagged AMPA receptor carboxy-terminal tails and Flag-tagged full-length rat SNX27. Again, we failed to observe a detectable association of AMPA receptor subunits with rat SNX27 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: No association of endogenous GluA1 or GluA2 with rat SNX27 was detected in primary rat cortical neuronal cultures.
source: Finally, to examine whether SNX27 could potentially interact with AMPA receptors specifically in the context of neurons we transduced primary rat cortical neuronal cultures with sindbis virus expressing either GFP or GFP-SNX27. Twenty-four hr after transduction we carried out GFP-nanotrap immunoisolation and quantitative western blotting for the endogenous AMPA receptor subunits GluA1 and GluA2. Again, under these conditions, we failed to detect any association of endogenous GluA1 or GluA2 with rat SNX27 (Figure 1H).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: The data is consistent with the SNX27-dependent recycling of AMPA receptors being principally controlled by indirect binding.
source: Together these data are consistent with the AMPA receptor PDZ binding motifs lacking the optimal sequence for high-affinity SNX27 binding (Clairfeuille et al., 2016) and corroborate our proteomic data. Whilst our data do not exclude that SNX27 may directly bind to AMPA receptors under specific circumstances, our data is more consistent with the SNX27-dependent recycling of AMPA receptors being principally controlled by indirect binding.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data and is supported by a citation to Clairfeuille et al., 2016.

claim: LRFN2 is a protein known to be involved in synaptic clustering.
source: Of particular interest in this regard was LRFN2, a protein known to be involved in synaptic clustering (Ko et al., 2006; Morimura et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Ko et al., 2006; Morimura et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2006.

claim: The LRFN family comprises five single transmembrane spanning proteins, LRFN1 through to LRFN5.
source: The LRFN family (also known as synaptic adhesion-like molecules [SALMs]) comprises five single transmembrane spanning proteins, LRFN1 through to LRFN5, that each contain an extracellular region of six leucine-rich repeats (LRR), an immunoglobulin (Ig) domain and a fibronectin type III domain, but differ in their cytosolic facing carboxy-terminal tails with LRFN1, LRFN2, and LRFN4 containing a Type I PDZ binding motif (Lie et al., 2018; Seabold et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Lie et al., 2018; Seabold et al., 2008.

claim: LRFN1, LRFN2, and LRFN4 contain a Type I PDZ binding motif.
source: The LRFN family (also known as synaptic adhesion-like molecules [SALMs]) comprises five single transmembrane spanning proteins, LRFN1 through to LRFN5, that each contain an extracellular region of six leucine-rich repeats (LRR), an immunoglobulin (Ig) domain and a fibronectin type III domain, but differ in their cytosolic facing carboxy-terminal tails with LRFN1, LRFN2, and LRFN4 containing a Type I PDZ binding motif (Lie et al., 2018; Seabold et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Lie et al., 2018; Seabold et al., 2008.

claim: LRFN1 and LRFN4 were identified in the raw SNX27 proteomic data sets but were filtered out from the final high confidence interactome because they were not quantified across all three biological repeats.
source: Both LRFN1 and LRFN4 were identified in the raw SNX27 proteomic data sets but were each filtered out from the final high confidence interactome because they were not quantified across all three biological repeats (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the proteomic results.

claim: Only those LRFNs containing a PDZ binding motif, LRFN1, LRFN2 and LRFN4, associated with endogenous SNX27.
source: Transient transfection into HEK293T cells followed by GFP-nanotrap immunoisolation of the GFP-LRFN fusion proteins and quantitative western blotting revealed that only those LRFNs containing a PDZ binding motif, LRFN1, LRFN2 and LRFN4, associated with endogenous SNX27 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Each association between LRFNs and SNX27 was dependent on the presence of the corresponding PDZ binding motif.
source: Moreover, each association was dependent on the presence of the corresponding PDZ binding motif as deletion of the last three amino acids resulted in mutant LRFNs that failed to associate with SNX27 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Mutation of the glutamic acid residue at the −3 position (LRFN2 (p.E786A)) or the carboxy-terminal valine (LRFN2 (p.V789A)) lead to the formation of mutant proteins that each lost the ability to associate with SNX27.
source: The LRFN2 PDZ binding motif is defined by the sequence E−3-S−2-T−1-V0, where the valine residue constitutes the carboxy-terminal amino acid. Mutation of the glutamic acid residue at the −3 position (LRFN2 (p.E786A)) or the carboxy-terminal valine (LRFN2 (p.V789A)) lead to the formation of mutant proteins that each lost the ability to associate with SNX27 (Figure 2C).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The isolated recombinant PDZ domain of SNX27 directly bound to a synthetic peptide corresponding to the LRFN2 PDZ binding motif with a high micromolar affinity (Kd = 1.6 µM).
source: This established that the isolated recombinant PDZ domain of SNX27 directly bound to a synthetic peptide corresponding to the LRFN2 PDZ binding motif, S-S-E-W-V-M-E−3-S-T-V−0 with a high micromolar affinity (Kd = 1.6 µM) (Figure 2D).
evidence: This statement is supported by ITC data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The affinity of the interaction between SNX27 PDZ domain and LRFN2 PDZ binding motif was enhanced upon inclusion of recombinant VPS26 (Kd < 1.0 µM).
source: Moreover, the affinity of this interaction was enhanced upon inclusion of recombinant VPS26 (Kd < 1.0 µM), a retromer component that directly associates with the PDZ domain of SNX27 and has been previously shown to enhance the binding affinity between the SNX27 PDZ domain and PDZ binding motif-containing peptides (Gallon et al., 2014; Chan et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by ITC data shown in Figure 2D and citations to Gallon et al., 2014; Chan et al., 2016.

claim: Endogenous LRFN2 associated with SNX27 in primary rat cortical neuronal cultures.
source: Finally, to confirm that endogenous LRFN2 also associated with SNX27, we transduced primary rat cortical neuronal cultures with sindbis virus expressing either GFP or GFP-SNX27. GFP-nanotrap immunoisolation and quantitative western blotting confirmed the association between SNX27 and full-length endogenous LRFN2 (Figure 2E).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: By means of its carboxy-terminal PDZ binding motif LRFN2 directly associates with the PDZ domain of SNX27.
source: Together these data establish that by means of its carboxy-terminal PDZ binding motif LRFN2 directly associates with the PDZ domain of SNX27.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: The endosome associated SNX27 co-localised with LRFN2 punctae throughout the neuron including in the dendrites and the cell body.
source: Confocal microscopy revealed that the endosome associated SNX27 (see Figure 1A) co-localised with LRFN2 punctae throughout the neuron including in the dendrites and the cell body (Figure 3A).
evidence: This statement is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The suppression of SNX27 expression led to a robust reduction in the total cellular level of LRFN2 (an approximate 50% reduction).
source: Similar to a wide array of other integral proteins that require endosomal SNX27 for their retrieval away from the lysosomal degradative fate (Steinberg et al., 2013), the suppression of SNX27 expression led to a robust reduction in the total cellular level of LRFN2 (an approximate 50% reduction, n = 5, unpaired t-test, t (8) = 4.6, p = 0.0017) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and a citation to Steinberg et al., 2013.

claim: The suppression of SNX27 expression led to a clear reduction in the cell surface level of GluA1 (an approximate 37% reduction).
source: Consistent with published studies (Hussain et al., 2014; Loo et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2013), the suppression of SNX27 expression led to a clear reduction in the cell surface level of GluA1 and GluA2 (an approximate 37% reduction for GluA1, n = 4, unpaired t-test, t (6) = 3.9, p = 0.0078; and an approximate 64% reduction for GluA2, n = 4, unpaired t-test, t (6) = 4.0, p = 0.0074) (Figure 3D).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and citations to Hussain et al., 2014; Loo et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2013.

claim: The suppression of SNX27 expression led to a clear reduction in the cell surface level of GluA2 (an approximate 64% reduction).
source: Consistent with published studies (Hussain et al., 2014; Loo et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2013), the suppression of SNX27 expression led to a clear reduction in the cell surface level of GluA1 and GluA2 (an approximate 37% reduction for GluA1, n = 4, unpaired t-test, t (6) = 3.9, p = 0.0078; and an approximate 64% reduction for GluA2, n = 4, unpaired t-test, t (6) = 4.0, p = 0.0074) (Figure 3D).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and citations to Hussain et al., 2014; Loo et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2013.

claim: Transferrin receptor levels were unchanged after SNX27 suppression.
source: Transferrin receptor levels were also measured as a control and were found to be unchanged (n = 4, unpaired t-test, t (6) = 0.6, p = 0.5774) (Figure 3E).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: SNX27 suppression induced a robust reduction in the cell surface level of LRFN2 (an approximate 52% reduction).
source: Importantly, under these conditions, SNX27 suppression also induced a robust reduction in the cell surface level of LRFN2 (an approximate 52% reduction, n = 6, unpaired t-test, t (10) = 5.0, p = 0.0006) (Figure 3F).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The colocalisation between LRFN2 and LAMP2 significantly increased after SNX27 suppression (an approximate 27% increase).
source: The colocalisation between LRFN2 and LAMP2 significantly increased after SNX27 suppression (an approximate 27% increase, n = 30, unpaired t-test, t (58) = 2.4, p = 0.0200) (Figure 3G).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: LRFN2 is an integral protein that requires SNX27 for its retrieval from lysosomal degradation, a pre-requisite for recycling back to the cell surface.
source: Together these data establish LRFN2 as an integral protein that conforms to the dogma of SNX27-mediated membrane trafficking in that it requires SNX27 for its retrieval from lysosomal degradation, a pre-requisite for recycling back to the cell surface.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: Research on LRFN2 has principally focused on its ability to cluster NMDA receptors.
source: For LRFN2, research has principally focused on its ability to cluster NMDA receptors (Wang et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2006.

claim: Points of overlap exist between the distribution of cell surface LRFN2 and endogenous GluA1 and GluA2 in dendrites.
source: This revealed points of overlap between the distribution of cell surface LRFN2 and endogenous GluA1 and GluA2 in dendrites (Figure 4A and B and C).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4A, B, and C.

claim: LRFN1, LRFN2, and LRFN4 were all able to associate with GluA1 and GluA2.
source: Twenty-four hr later GFP-nanotrap immunoisolation (targeting the SEP tag) and western analysis revealed that LRFN1, LRFN2, and LRFN4 were all able to associate with GluA1 and GluA2 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Deletion of the LRR and Ig domains of LRFN2 led to a reduction in binding to GluA1 (an approximate 56% reduction) and GluA2 (an approximate 67% reduction).
source: While full-length LRFN2 associated with GluA1 and GluA2, deletion of the LRR and Ig domains led to a reduction in binding (an approximate 56% reduction for GluA1, n = 4, unpaired t-test, t (6) = 3.3, p = 0.0173; and an approximate 67% reduction for GluA2, n = 4, unpaired t-test, t (6) = 10.6, p = <0.0001) that was further reduced upon removal of the juxtamembrane fibronectin type III domain (an approximate 79% reduction for GluA1, n = 4, unpaired t-test, t (6) = 12.8, p = <0.0001; and an approximate 94% reduction for GluA2, n = 4, unpaired t-test, t (6) = 40.5, p = <0.0001) (Figure 4F).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: LRFN2 and AMPA receptors show overlapping distributions on the cell surface of dendrites.
source: Taken together, this data demonstrates that LRFN2 and AMPA receptors show overlapping distributions on the cell surface of dendrites, and that LRFN2 associates with the GluA1 and GluA2 subunits of AMPA receptors through an interaction principally mediated by its extracellular LRR and Ig domains.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: SNX27 suppression caused a significant reduction in cell surface GluA1 staining (an approximate 16% reduction).
source: Consistent with the aforementioned biochemical analysis this revealed a significant reduction in cell surface GluA1 and GluA2 staining upon SNX27 suppression (GluA1: an approximate 16% reduction, n = 50, Mann Whitney test, U (730), p = 0.0003; GluA2: an approximate 34% reduction n = 50, Mann Whitney test, U (632), p < 0.0001) (Figure 5A).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: SNX27 suppression caused a significant reduction in cell surface GluA2 staining (an approximate 34% reduction).
source: Consistent with the aforementioned biochemical analysis this revealed a significant reduction in cell surface GluA1 and GluA2 staining upon SNX27 suppression (GluA1: an approximate 16% reduction, n = 50, Mann Whitney test, U (730), p = 0.0003; GluA2: an approximate 34% reduction n = 50, Mann Whitney test, U (632), p < 0.0001) (Figure 5A).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The suppression of LRFN2 expression caused a significant reduction in GluA2 surface expression (an approximate 40% reduction).
source: In a parallel analysis, the suppression of LRFN2 expression (Figure 5B) also caused a significant reduction in GluA2 surface expression (an approximate 40% reduction, n = 50, Mann Whitney test, U (556), p < 0.0001) but, interestingly, had no significant effect on the cell surface expression of GluA1 (n = 50, Mann Whitney test, U (1228), p = 0.8813) (Figure 5C).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The suppression of LRFN2 expression had no significant effect on the cell surface expression of GluA1.

claim: The intensity of internalised GluA2 was significantly increased after suppression of SNX27 (an approximate 43% increase).
source: The intensity of internalised GluA2 was quantified in the cell body and proximal dendrites and found to be significantly increased after suppression of both SNX27 (an approximate 43% increase, n = 58, Mann Whitney test, U (827), p < 0.0001) and LRFN2 (an approximate 14% increase, n = 58, Mann Whitney test, U (1198), p = 0.0073) with the GluA2 overlapping with both VPS35 and LAMP1 (Figure 6A, B, C).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6A, B, C.

claim: The intensity of internalised GluA2 was significantly increased after suppression of LRFN2 (an approximate 14% increase).

claim: Suppression of SNX27 or LRFN2 perturbs the recycling of GluA2, increasing its retention time in the endo-lysosomal system.

evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data presented.

claim: SNX27 shRNA treatment profoundly decreased excitatory synaptic transmission compared to the non-targeting control shRNA.
source: Input-output curves showed that SNX27 shRNA treatment profoundly decreased excitatory synaptic transmission compared to the non-targeting control shRNA (two-way repeated-measures ANOVA, between subjects, F (1,19) = 22.3, p = 0.0001) (Figure 7B and C).
evidence: This statement is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 7B and C.

claim: LRFN2 shRNA treatment significantly decreased excitatory synaptic transmission compared to the non-targeting control shRNA.
source: Importantly, LRFN2 shRNA treatment also significantly decreased excitatory synaptic transmission compared to the non-targeting control shRNA (two-way repeated-measures ANOVA, between subjects F (1,12) = 6.7, p = 0.024) (Figure 7D and E).
evidence: This statement is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 7D and E.

claim: SNX27 produced a larger reduction in glutamatergic transmission than LRFN2 suppression.
source: A direct comparison of LRFN2 and SNX27 phenotypes revealed that SNX27 produced a larger reduction in glutamatergic transmission than LRFN2 suppression (two-way repeated-measures ANOVA, between subjects F (1,16) = 4.6, p = 0.047) (Figure 7F), whereas there was no difference in transmission between the two non-targeting control shRNAs (F (1,15) = 0.95, p = 0.35), suggesting that SNX27, as well as affecting LRFN2 expression, may also be regulating other LRFNs and/or other synaptic proteins that can influence AMPA receptor activity.
evidence: This statement is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: Loss of SNX27 has previously been shown to impair induction of hippocampal LTP.
source: Finally, loss of SNX27 has previously been shown to impair induction of hippocampal LTP (Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2013.

claim: Non-targeting control-treated slices exhibited robust LTP following high-frequency stimulation.
source: Following high-frequency stimulation (HFS), we observed that the non-targeting control-treated slices exhibited robust LTP (paired t-test, t (5) = 3.9, p = 0.011) (Figure 7G and H) while no detectable LTP was induced in the LRFN2 shRNA-treated slices (paired t-test, t (4) = 1.8, p = 0.15) (Figure 7G and I) indicating that LRFN2 suppression attenuates the induction of LTP.
evidence: This statement is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 7G and H.

claim: No detectable LTP was induced in the LRFN2 shRNA-treated slices.

claim: LRFN2 plays an important role in the functional expression and activity of synaptic AMPA receptors.
source: Taken together these data indicate that LRFN2 plays an important role in the functional expression and activity of synaptic AMPA receptors and reveals a new player in the complex SNX27-mediated regulation of AMPA receptor trafficking.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: AMPA receptors are one of the major types of ionotropic glutamate receptors present at the postsynaptic density of excitatory synapses.
source: AMPA receptors are one of the major types of ionotropic glutamate receptors present at the postsynaptic density of excitatory synapses and, consequently, perturbed AMPA receptor trafficking has been implicated in numerous neurological and psychiatric disorders (Henley and Wilkinson, 2016, Shankar et al., 2008, Shepherd and Huganir, 2007, Walsh et al., 2002, Grooms et al., 2000, Yamashita and Kwak, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Perturbed AMPA receptor trafficking has been implicated in numerous neurological and psychiatric disorders.

claim: Four core AMPA receptor subunits, GluA1 through to GluA4, combine to produce functionally diverse homo- and hetero-tetrameric channels which drive fast excitatory synaptic transmission.
source: Four core AMPA receptor subunits, GluA1 through to GluA4, combine to produce functionally diverse homo- and hetero-tetrameric channels which drive fast excitatory synaptic transmission (Hollmann and Heinemann, 1994, Henley and Wilkinson, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Hollmann and Heinemann, 1994, Henley and Wilkinson, 2016.

claim: AMPA receptors utilise membrane trafficking pathways to dynamically regulate their number, composition, and biophysical properties at the postsynaptic membrane during the modulation of synaptic strength associated with learning and memory.
source: AMPA receptors utilise membrane trafficking pathways to dynamically regulate their number, composition, and biophysical properties at the postsynaptic membrane during the modulation of synaptic strength associated with learning and memory (Henley and Wilkinson, 2016; Diering and Huganir, 2018; Huganir and Nicoll, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Henley and Wilkinson, 2016; Diering and Huganir, 2018; Huganir and Nicoll, 2013.

claim: LRFN2 is increasingly being linked to a range of neurological conditions including antisocial personality disorder, autism, schizophrenia, working memory deficits, and learning disabilities.
source: LRFN2 is increasingly being linked to a range of neurological conditions including antisocial personality disorder (Rautiainen et al., 2016), autism (Morimura et al., 2017), schizophrenia (Morimura et al., 2017), working memory deficits, and learning disabilities (Thevenon et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Rautiainen et al., 2016; Morimura et al., 2017; Thevenon et al., 2016.

claim: A recent proteomic screen on pre-frontal post-mortem tissue revealed that LRFN2 protein expression was significantly decreased in people with Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease with dementia, and dementia with Lewy bodies.
source: A recent proteomic screen on pre-frontal post-mortem tissue also revealed that LRFN2 protein expression was significantly decreased in people with Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease with dementia, and dementia with Lewy bodies, further highlighting the importance of LRFN2 for neuronal function (Bereczki et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Bereczki et al., 2018.

claim: LRFN2 had the highest level of reduction compared to other synaptic proteins in all three forms of dementia, and its loss was strongly associated with rate of cognitive decline.
source: LRFN2 had the highest level of reduction compared to other synaptic proteins in all three forms of dementia, and its loss was strongly associated with rate of cognitive decline (Bereczki et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Bereczki et al., 2018.

claim: Suppression of SNX27 leads to a reduction in LRFN2 expression which results in a loss of surface expression of GluA2 and, correspondingly, a loss of synaptic activity.
source: In summary, we have identified LRFN2 as a high-affinity neuronal interactor of SNX27 that is required for AMPA receptor-mediated synaptic transmission. Suppression of SNX27 leads to a reduction in LRFN2 expression which results in a loss of surface expression of GluA2 and, correspondingly, a loss of synaptic activity (Figure 8).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented and is illustrated in Figure 8.

claim: The link between SNX27, LRFN2, and AMPA receptors provides a new point of control for AMPA receptor-mediated synaptic transmission and plasticity.
source: The link between SNX27, LRFN2, and AMPA receptors provides a new point of control for AMPA receptor-mediated synaptic transmission and plasticity and provides additional insight into the association of LRFN2 and SNX27 with many neurological and psychiatric conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.
